affected_groups: communities competing for pasture and water
alternative_explanations: Non-climatic resource-governance drivers are not isolated.
uncertainty: Government synthesis, not event-specific causal estimation. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
compact_statement: Drought can intensify water/pasture competition and intercommunity conflict.

climate_pressure: Drought, heat and unreliable rainfall described in Turkana's May 2023 assessment.
documented_impact: Reduced dry-season pasture and water availability undermine pastoral livelihoods.
fcv_mediator: Competition over grazing land and livestock water interacts with political, environmental and economic challenges.
possible_consequence: The county assessment describes heightened likelihood of conflict and insecurity, not an inevitable violent outcome.
alternative_explanations: Political marginalization, land access, existing insecurity and economic change can independently shape competition and violence.
uncertainty: Source-stated qualitative mechanism dated 2023; no causal effect size, event attribution or 2026 conflict prediction. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Community groups and county support are reported resource-management capacities; effects and inclusive access were not independently evaluated.
compact_statement: Turkana's 2023 assessment links drought-related pasture/water loss with competition and heightened insecurity, mediated by existing governance and livelihood pressures.
